newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf Arab gold demand up 17 percent in 1Q 1997.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Arab gold demand up 17 percent in 1Q 1997.

text.p: Demand for gold in Gulf Arab state's climbed by 17 percent in the first quarter of 1997 compared to the same period in the previous year, reaching 33.7 tonnes, the World Gold Council (WGC) said on Wednesday.

A WGC statement -- covering the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman and Qatar -- said jewellery demand also rose by 17 percent to 28 tonnes and investment gold demand increased by 20 percent to 5.1 tonnes.
The UAE, a key gold customer in the oil-rich Gulf, saw stronger demand, registering a new quarterly record of 16.9 tonnes, said the statement from the WGC's Dubai office.
In Oman, first quarter demand climbed by 17 percent to reach 4.8 tonnes.
Bahrain's appetite for gold amounted to 2.6 tonnes and Qatari demand reached 2.2 tonnes.
Kuwait's demand for gold dropped 11 percent to 7.2 tonnes, the statement said.
"The decline represented a return to more sustainable levels following two years of exceptionally strong demand in 1995 and 1996," the statement said.
The Geneva-based WGC is a non-profit association owned by major gold producers and monitors about 75 percent of the world's markets.
